description: This case study builds prototypical office building energy models for South Korea and uses them to evaluate national building energy policy. It is published in Sustainability (24 March 2021) by Hye-Jin Kim and Donghyun Seo of Chungbuk National University and Do-Young Choi of the Korea Energy Economics Institute (KEEI). Korea mandated zero-energy construction for residential buildings from 2025 and non-residential buildings from 2030, and two decades after its building energy policies began, few studies had examined the energy use of the non-residential stock. The authors defined prototypical offices from KEEI's first large-scale non-residential building survey, built a detailed energy model, verified its estimates against observed consumption, and applied it in a policy evaluation. Coverage: Korea's office building stock as represented in the survey. Access: open-access article with PDF. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: the survey microdata are not published with the article, and the prototype represents an average office. Simulation uses: prototype models for national energy and emissions scenarios and for testing codes and zero-energy mandates. Related records: the Eurac baseline building models and EnergyPlus.
